answer.evidence: The sprigs are thin stalks drawn in flat elevation, with no horizontal surface. Each soil strip is only 2 rows: row 6 (or 13) is a lighter 1-row rim and row 7 (or 14) is a dark row. These have no ellipse, no band that ends in an edge line with eave shadow, and no visible heap or contents. The widths are constant at 32 for 2 rows each, so the strips read as thin front-facing ledges. The whole piece is a flat front view of plants on a thin base.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, sparse row of dead crop stalks, about two rows of short brown sticks on soil, and only 6 distinct colours in total. The references are full trees with 5-6+ green steps, clustered leaf texture, and a shaded trunk. The candidate has about 2-3 tones and no canopy or clump shading, so it is much thinner than the references. It is sparse by nature, so I did not fail it on the per-tile measured counts, which read 0 because the piece is smaller than a tile. By eye, though, it looks flatter and thinner than either reference. The sticks are single-tone with little grain, and the soil strip has little variation. There are no tinted outlines or material-tone edges, and the 0% neutral edge share is just because there are almost no dark edge pixels. A careful artist would not accept this next to the references without it looking like a thin sticker-like sketch. Verdict: fail.
